headline: High risk of filesystem-based prompt injection and write conflicts; no evidence of direct data leakage or compliance mismatch.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Mentat reads and writes files and shares state via filesystem, so Prefect can ingest Mentat-produced artifacts if orchestrated together. Prefect’s documented API/orchestration role makes it plausible as a downstream consumer, but no direct shared channel or parser is shown. The interaction exists in default filesystem-based workflows, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF Prefect consumes files or workflow metadata produced by Mentat without provenance checks, injection is possible.
IF the two agents are connected through a shared workspace, attacker-controlled file content can bridge them.
mitigations: Add a provenance header check before Prefect reads Mentat outputs.
Restrict Mentat output directories to non-executable, review-only paths.
Use separate workspaces for the two agents.
Require manual approval before Prefect acts on any Mentat-generated artifact.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Mentat can read selected files and sends context to a configured model provider, while Prefect only shows API calls to GitHub and workflow metadata handling. The pair does not show a shared sensitive-data workspace or authenticated shared principal, so leakage is limited and not default. The main risk is accidental exposure of source code through Mentat’s provider calls.
conditions: IF Mentat is pointed at files containing secrets or regulated data, those contents may be sent to its model provider.
IF Prefect is configured to ingest the same workspace, metadata may reveal filenames or workflow structure.
mitigations: Exclude secret-bearing files from Mentat input paths.
Use a redaction pre-pass before any model-provider call.
Keep Prefect and Mentat on separate repositories or mounts.
Rotate any exposed API keys if sensitive files were already processed.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Mentat has write_filesystem and modify_git_state, and its concurrency model says shared state with other instances is via filesystem. Prefect is an orchestration system with broad network egress and workflow automation, so if it also mutates the same repo or workspace, concurrent writes can corrupt state. Because the shared mutable surface is explicit and defaults are dangerous, high is warranted.
conditions: IF Prefect writes to the same repository or workspace that Mentat edits, concurrent modification conflicts can occur.
IF both agents operate without locking on shared files or git state, last-writer-wins corruption is possible.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate checkout.
Enable file or git locking around shared paths.
Serialize write phases so only one agent mutates state at a time.
Have Prefect operate read-only on Mentat-managed repositories.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Mentat produces diff-based edit proposals, and Prefect can orchestrate downstream workflows that may consume those outputs. If Prefect treats Mentat’s artifacts as authoritative without verification, errors can cascade into automated workflow actions. The pathway exists, but the profiles do not show direct destructive actions by default, so medium fits.
conditions: IF Prefect uses Mentat-generated diffs or notes as authoritative inputs, unverified mistakes can propagate.
IF Prefect triggers downstream jobs based on those artifacts, the error can affect multiple work products.
mitigations: Insert a human review step before Prefect consumes Mentat outputs.
Validate diffs against tests or schema checks before orchestration.
Require Prefect to read only signed or checksum-verified artifacts.
Log and alert on any automated action sourced from Mentat output.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and only explicitly touch source code or workflow metadata, with no stated PHI, EU PII, or residency mismatch. Mentat’s model-provider API calls could create policy obligations, but Prefect’s profile does not show a conflicting compliance regime. The evidence is insufficient for a stronger finding, so low is appropriate.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into Mentat inputs, provider-side handling may create compliance obligations.
IF Prefect is configured with retention or residency rules different from Mentat’s provider, policy mismatch can arise.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both agents’ inputs.
Document retention and residency settings for the model provider.
Add a short data-classification checklist before runs.
Review vendor terms before processing sensitive repositories.
